newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian canola crush margins seen improving - trade.
newsitem.headline: Canadian canola crush margins seen improving - trade.

text.p: Canadian canola crush margins should improve in the next month on better-than-expected production prospects in canola and higher soybean meal and oil values, crushers said.

"Crush margins have turned favourably with the pressure on canola and the strength in soybean oil and meal. We expect more of that to happen as harvest pressure and old crop carry out start materializing over the next month or so," said Bijay Kumar, products manager of U.S.-based Cargill Inc's Cargill Ltd's newest crush plant in Clavet, Sask.
Canola crushers hedge their risk by buying Winnipeg Commodity Exchange canola futures and selling Chicago Board of Trade soybean meal and oil futures.
WCE canola futures closed C$1.50 to C$3 a tonne lower Tuesday while CBOT soyoil closed up US$0.11 to US$0.32 per lb and soymeal close US$1 to US$2.30 a ton higher.
Canadian cash crush margins Tuesday were between C$5 to C$10 a tonne, Kumar said.
"That's just around variable crush costs. We're not going to go full out on our crush, these margins are not attractive. It's been pretty bad at the end of the crop year," he said.
